options.A: It can be tested only with tracer gases such as helium or ammonia, and must be done for every batch; the pressure drop method is not accepted, and it is repeated every year
options.B: It need be measured only at normal operating pressure, with no pressure increase, and only the constant pressure method is to be used
options.C: A soap-solution test at installation is enough, with no further testing unless there is major repair or glove replacement
options.D: It can be tested by a pressure drop or constant pressure test, usually at twice the operating pressure

questions.explanation: The document explains that after the enclosure is closed with airtight blanking plates, a pressure drop or constant pressure test can be used, usually at twice the operating pressure. Tracer gases (such as helium or ammonia) or soap solution can be used at installation to locate leaks, but they are not suitable for routine use.

questions.question: A facility makes a product for export to another country. What is the principle of ISPE Vol. 3 regarding environmental and safety legislation?

options.A: Only the importing country's regulations need be met and the manufacturing country's can be ignored, because the product is not sold locally
options.B: The facility must still comply with the regulations of the country where it is located, even if the product is exported; the manufacturing country's regulations may be stricter
options.C: Only US and EU regulations need be met, since they are the strictest in the world, and other countries do not apply
options.D: Meeting GMP is regarded as meeting all environmental and safety regulations, with no separate check needed

questions.explanation: The document stresses that a facility must comply with the regulations of the country where it is located even if the product is exported, and some regulations of the manufacturing country may be stricter than those of the importing country. It also warns that a process may fully comply with GMP and still violate other regulations if environmental impact was not considered in design, so engineering solutions must consider both GEP and GMP.

questions.question: To reduce wastewater volume, the document recommends a "water quality cascade". Which of the following is an example the document gives?

options.A: Discard the final rinse water and use fresh WFI as the first wash water, to ensure consistent cleaning quality every time
options.B: Recover process wastewater containing active ingredients directly as WFI feed water, treated by RO before use
options.C: Discharge process wastewater directly to the municipal sewer, to reduce the treatment facility burden and reduce in-plant water use, rather than recycling
options.D: WFI blow down as boiler feed water; final rinse water as first wash water; RO reject water for irrigation

questions.explanation: The concept of a water quality cascade is to reuse cleaner water streams for lower-specification uses, for example WFI blow down as boiler feed water, final rinse as first wash, and RO reject as irrigation water. Biologically active wastewater must be handled in a high-integrity manner, treated as a GMP system.

questions.question: Fire sprinkler heads in clean areas can affect cleaning and the maintenance of room pressure. What practice does the document recommend?

options.A: Use sprinkler heads that are flush with the ceiling and sealed (sealed and concealed), or use other means of fire protection
options.B: Use exposed sprinkler heads, to ease later inspection and replacement, with openings left in the clean area and connected by exposed piping
options.C: Prohibit any fire protection equipment in clean areas, with adjacent rooms handling fire protection, to avoid contamination
options.D: Open the ceiling and install the piping, with no special sealing treatment, strengthening it later if needed

questions.explanation: Sprinkler systems create cleaning and air leakage problems, so sprinkler heads that keep flush with the ceiling profile and are sealed to the ceiling (sealed and concealed) are recommended, and other means of fire protection can also be specified as appropriate. This bears directly on the cleanability of the clean area and on maintaining pressure.

questions.question: In an aseptic facility, the need for emergency egress can conflict with the need to maintain pressure differentials and protect the product. How does the document recommend handling this?

options.A: Even during egress the gowning procedure must be followed and airlocks not bypassed, to avoid breaking cleanliness, even in a fire alarm
options.B: Rely on personnel training alone, with no special design provision, and decide on site during egress
options.C: Door interlocks should be able to be overridden in an emergency, and doors are recommended to be fail safe (unlocked on loss of power)
options.D: Keep all doors normally open to ensure free passage in an emergency, and compensate the pressure loss with airflow velocity, for maximum safety

questions.explanation: The document notes that the design must overcome the conflict between complex entry and exit procedures (to maintain pressure cascades) and escape routes; emergency exits should not conflict with clean area requirements, door interlocks must be overridable when necessary, and doors are recommended to be fail safe, releasing on loss of power in an emergency. Personnel safety takes priority over clean area procedures.

questions.question: In site selection, which item does ISPE Vol. 3 treat as the primary requirement for a sterile products facility?

options.A: Proximity to energy sources such as natural gas and electricity, to reduce operating costs, because it can reduce costs
options.B: Ambient air quality
options.C: Local government officials' familiarity with the relevant regulations and the permit review process
options.D: Tolerance of the surrounding community for noise and traffic

questions.explanation: The document states that ambient air quality is the primary requirement in site selection for a sterile products plant; if the site is in an industrial or agricultural area, the effect of these activities should be considered, and before selecting the site the air can be sampled and analyzed for undesirable concentrations of chemicals and dust. A natural gas source is an advantage but not the primary one, and noise and regulatory staff familiarity are other considerations.

questions.question: In cleanroom design, for which in-operation environmental grade is each of the two approaches, "dilution" and "displacement", suitable?

options.A: An ISO 7/Grade B background can be achieved by turbulent dilution; ISO 5/Grade A is achieved by displacement (UAF)
options.B: ISO 5/Grade A can be achieved by turbulent dilution; ISO 7/Grade B needs a displacement system (UAF)
options.C: Both can achieve ISO 5/Grade A, differing mainly in energy consumption and initial investment cost
options.D: Both can achieve only ISO 8/Grade C, and anything above ISO 7 must use an isolator

questions.explanation: The document states that in operation ISO 7/Grade B can be achieved by turbulent airflow dilution, while ISO 5/Grade A needs a displacement system (UAF, replacing dirty air with cleaner air). A displacement cleanroom has air change rates up to hundreds per hour and is costly, so it is reserved for the highest-risk ISO 5/Grade A areas.

questions.question: Among the four basic requirements for turbulent dilution cleanrooms, what does the document require of the location of the extract?

options.A: The extract should be high on the ceiling so air flows upward and carries particles away, adjacent to the supply to save ducting
options.B: The extract position does not matter as long as the air change rate is met, regardless of the room airflow pattern
options.C: The extract should be at a low level to remove particles effectively, otherwise the air changes may merely be exhausting clean air
options.D: The extract should be concentrated at a single point in the middle of the room, to create the strongest airflow and shorten the air change time

questions.explanation: The document lists four requirements for dilution rooms: the supply air is significantly cleaner than the room, the extract is at a low level, the supply air mixes almost completely with the room air, and the supply airflow is enough to offset the particle generation. If the extract is badly located, the air change calculation is based on exhausting clean air, which a smoke test can reveal; a high-level return disrupts the airflow pattern and is not recommended.

questions.question: A room of 1000 ft3 has a supply airflow of 400 ft3/min (CFM). Using the calculation method in the document, what is the air change rate (ACH) of this room?

options.A: 2.4 ACH
options.B: 12 ACH
options.C: 40 ACH
options.D: 24 ACH

questions.explanation: ACH = hourly supply airflow / room volume = 400 x 60 / 1000 = 24. The document also notes that this airflow may be less than what is needed to cool the room, so the actual airflow must consider all three of heat load, particle generation and required recovery time, taking the most stringent.

questions.question: According to the document's simplified model, about how long does it take to recover from ISO 7/Grade B to ISO 5/Grade A levels (a 100-fold recovery) at 20 ACH?

options.A: About 5 minutes
options.B: About 14 minutes
options.C: About 30 minutes
options.D: About 60 minutes

questions.explanation: The document uses a simple exponential decay model to show that a 100-fold recovery takes about 14 minutes at 20 ACH and about 9 minutes at 30 ACH; the model assumes good mixing and particle-free supply air. The document also notes that achieving the target recovery time is usually more important than achieving the target air change rate.

questions.question: What problem arises if the high-temperature HEPA filter of a depyrogenation tunnel is operated above its rated temperature (burned in)?

options.A: Filter efficiency increases, because high temperature makes the media denser, so service life can be extended
options.B: The filter only needs an added pre-filter to restore its rated performance, with no repeat leak test
options.C: The media binder may decompose, and the filter often fails the leak scan
options.D: The filter automatically passes the leak test, because high temperature eliminates all microbial and particle leaks

questions.explanation: Traditional high-temperature HEPA has an upper limit of 250 degC (482 degF), while many depyrogenation tunnels and ovens run hotter. Once a filter is operated above its rated temperature, the media binder starts to decompose and the filter often fails the leak test scan, so other ways are needed to verify low particle levels in the hot zone; newer high-temperature HEPA claims to withstand higher temperatures and allow continued leak testing.

questions.question: What does the document recommend for the in situ leak testing of HEPA filters?

options.A: Both UAF HEPA filters and AHU main filters need only a single-point downstream test, with no upstream challenge concentration data
options.B: No HEPA filter needs to be tested at operating airflow, to reduce test time, and testing need be done only when shut down
options.C: Upstream challenge particles can be obtained by puncturing the filter to create holes, to ensure enough concentration, with repair after the test and no retest
options.D: UAF HEPA filters need a full face scan; AHU main filters can be tested at a single point when the downstream is well mixed

questions.explanation: UAF HEPA filters should be fully scanned to ensure air quality over the whole downstream filter face; the downstream airflow of an AHU main filter is turbulent and already mixed, so a single-point test is enough if there is sufficient downstream distance, and what matters is the overall efficiency. HEPA filters should be tested at their operating airflow, and upstream challenge particles must not be obtained by damaging the filter.

questions.question: Regulations and guidance often cite a UAF velocity of about 90 ft/min (0.45 m/s) +/- 20% (measured 100-150 mm below the filter). How does ISPE Vol. 3 view this value?

options.A: It should not be treated as a critical release criterion; the velocity for a specific application should be determined by design and evaluation and shown to be effective, and may be as low as about half
options.B: It is a scientifically proven absolute minimum for protecting product, and no application may go below it
options.C: It applies only to ISO 8/Grade C rooms, and ISO 5/Grade A has different requirements
options.D: As long as CFD simulation passes, velocity and airflow patterns need not be measured again at validation

questions.explanation: The document explains that this value originates from Federal Standard 209, has no scientific link to the product protection effect of UAF, and should not be used as a critical acceptance criterion; FDA guidance suggests it be determined by design according to the application. ISO 14644-4 also mentions examples of velocities down to about half applied successfully, and with obstacles a lower velocity can reduce turbulence. CFD can be used in design, but airflow patterns must still be evaluated on site at validation.

questions.question: How is the alarm delay for room differential pressure usually set?

options.A: No delay, with an alarm as soon as the pressure differential deviates, to ensure maximum safety, and shutdown at every door opening
options.B: Usually a few minutes (generally less than 10 minutes), supported by study data on door opening and pressure loss
options.C: 30 to 60 minutes, because loss of differential pressure does not affect room cleanliness and needs no investigation
options.D: 24 hours, with alarm records reviewed daily and no need for real-time notification of personnel

questions.explanation: Room differential pressure is a regulatory expectation but not necessarily a primary critical process parameter; a loss of pressure does not necessarily mean a loss of cleanliness, so the delay is usually a few minutes (generally less than 10 minutes), supported by studies of the time needed to open a door and the maximum duration of pressure loss, and the time for conditions to be lost after an HVAC failure should be observed to ensure the delay value is safe.

questions.question: Which pressure differential control method is sensitive to doors opening and closing, often freezes control with a door switch when the door is open, and suits variable airflow situations such as isolators?

options.A: Fixed Offset (fixed offset airflow control)
options.B: Tracking Control (tracking airflow control)
options.C: Direct Pressure Control
options.D: Fixed (Hard) Balanced (fixed balanced airflow)

questions.explanation: Direct Pressure Control uses a pressure control loop to adjust return or exhaust dampers automatically, self-correcting even when room airflow or leakage changes, but it is sensitive to doors opening and closing, so door switches are used to freeze control, and it is especially suited to variable airflow situations such as isolators. Fixed Offset and Tracking are not sensitive to door operation, and Fixed Balanced is passive control that is cheap and easy to maintain.

questions.question: Which statement about the basic features of a pass-through box is correct?

options.A: The doors at both ends must be interlocked so they cannot both be open; it differs from a material airlock in that no personnel ever enter it
options.B: The doors at both ends need only have indicator lights, and whether to interlock is left to the user, with no qualification and no records needed
options.C: It must have active ventilation and automatic disinfection, otherwise it may not be used in any aseptic area
options.D: It must use fully airtight gaskets to be used in ordinary GMP areas, and be leak tested daily

questions.explanation: A pass-through box has doors at both ends that must be interlocked so they cannot be opened at the same time, and should be easy to clean and resistant to cleaning agents; unlike a material airlock, it never lets personnel enter, so its interior can be smooth and easy to clean, small, and of lower risk to the cleanroom. Ventilation, disinfection, timed interlocks and airtight gaskets are optional features, and airtight gaskets are normally used only in the most hazardous applications (such as BSL-4).

questions.question: According to the ISPE Vol. 3 glossary, how is a Controlled Not Classified (CNC) area defined?

options.A: An area with airborne particle limits but no need for microbial monitoring
options.B: An area with no airborne particle limits but with filtered ventilation
options.C: A storage area with no ventilation or environmental control at all
options.D: A temporary area where environmental control is activated only during batch production

questions.explanation: The glossary defines CNC as an area "without airborne particle limits but with filtered ventilation". It differs from an Unclassified Area (such as warehouses, offices and other support areas around manufacturing) and is not a classified space with particle limits (which implies ongoing environmental monitoring).

questions.question: According to the glossary, a sterilizing filter is defined by which microorganism and what challenge concentration?

options.A: Bacillus subtilis, at a challenge of 10^3 per cm2 of membrane area
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, at a challenge of 10^5 per cm2 of membrane area
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus, at a challenge of 10^6 per cm2 of membrane area
options.D: Brevundimonas diminuta, at a challenge of at least 10^7 per cm2

questions.explanation: The glossary defines a sterilizing filter as a filter that produces a sterile filtrate when challenged with at least 10^7 organisms/cm2 of membrane area of Brevundimonas diminuta. The other organisms and lower concentrations are not in this definition.

questions.question: A cleanroom is complete, with equipment installed and operating as agreed, but no personnel are in the room. According to ISO 14644-1 and the glossary, which state is this?

options.A: As-Built
options.B: In Operation
options.C: At Rest
options.D: Normal Operating Condition

questions.explanation: At Rest means the cleanroom is complete, with equipment installed and operating as agreed, but with no personnel. As-Built is when all services are connected and functioning but there is no production equipment, materials or personnel; In Operation is when equipment operates as specified with the specified number of personnel present; Normal Operating Condition is the normal range of values of a parameter, not a room occupancy state.

questions.question: According to the glossary, what is the difference in the definitions of RABS and isolator?

options.A: RABS is an "enclosed, but not closed" environment separated from the outside by rigid walls and air overspill; an isolator is decontaminated and continuously isolated from the outside
options.B: RABS is a fully closed system that allows no air overspill; an isolator relies on air overspill and rigid walls for separation, and neither can be decontaminated
options.C: The two definitions are identical and only the names differ, the difference being only vendor marketing terms and equipment size
options.D: RABS can operate only in ISO 8/Grade C and may not use gloves; an isolator can operate only in ISO 7/Grade B

questions.explanation: The glossary defines a RABS as an enclosed but not closed system of rigid walls plus air overspill that provides ISO 5/Grade A conditions; an isolator is a unit that is decontaminated, meets ISO 5/Grade A, and continuously isolates its interior from the surrounding environment, and can be open or closed.

questions.question: According to the glossary, how is the efficiency of a HEPA filter defined?

options.A: More than 99.0% efficiency for 0.5 um particles
options.B: More than 99.9% efficiency for 0.1 um particles (ULPA grade)
options.C: More than 99.99% efficiency for 5 um particles
options.D: More than 99.97% efficiency for 0.3 um particles

questions.explanation: The glossary defines HEPA as a filter with more than 99.97% efficiency for 0.3 um particles; by contrast, ULPA is an Ultra Low Penetration Air filter. The document also notes that a HEPA filter captures more than 99.97% of particles both larger and smaller than 0.3 um.
questions.reference: ISPE Vol.3 §13.2 Glossary: High Efficiency Particulate Air (HEPA) Filter
